name: National Association of Realtors homepage: a navigation page, not a technology study
title: National Association of Realtors homepage: a navigation page, not a technology study
answer: This is the homepage of the National Association of Realtors, an American trade association covering residential and commercial real estate. It is a navigation page rather than a report, so it offers no findings of its own. Its most useful element for an AI reader is a menu entry pointing to technology content, described as data on the latest trends and statistics that members can use to improve their business. The page confirms that NAR publishes technology material but does not itself contain any survey results or adoption figures.

sections.body: The National Association of Realtors publishes this page. It is the organisation's main website homepage, harvested on 27 September 2026, and it describes NAR as an American trade association involved in all aspects of residential and commercial real estate. The page is a menu of links rather than a document, covering member resources, training, news, events, policy updates, trademark rules, the Realtors Political Action Committee, designations and certifications, and a technology section. No author, publication date or report title is given.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page states that NAR is an American trade association involved in all aspects of residential and commercial real estate. It presents a set of submenus. One says that whether you are a new agent or an experienced broker you have access to a wide array of resources designed to help you succeed in today's market. Another lists the areas the site covers, including home buying and selling, commercial, international, NAR member information, and technology, and says to use the data to improve your business through knowledge of the latest trends and statistics. A further entry notes that NAR and its affiliated Institutes, Societies, and Councils offer a wide selection of real estate training options. Others cover staying current on industry issues with daily news, networking, seminars and events, policy updates for Realtors, MLSs, brokers, buyers and sellers, trademark rules stating that only members of NAR can call themselves a Realtor, the Realtors Political Action Committee, and designations and certifications that increase skills, proficiency and knowledge to help boost salary and client base. Several of these descriptions repeat verbatim elsewhere on the page.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, no survey results and no adoption rates. The specific positions it does state are that NAR is an American trade association involved in all aspects of residential and commercial real estate, that only members of NAR can call themselves a Realtor, and that the site covers home buying and selling, commercial, international, member information and technology.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in real estate would use this page only as a pointer. It confirms that NAR treats technology as one of its subject areas and claims to publish data on the latest trends and statistics, which is where technology research such as member surveys would sit. The page itself contains none of that research, so it cannot support any statement about which AI tools agents or brokerages adopt. It is useful for locating the publisher and its technology section, not for evidence.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: This is a commercial and promotional homepage for a membership trade association, not a study. It is undated beyond the harvest date, has no named author, and its substance is navigation labels, several of which repeat. It does not cover AI tools, adoption rates, brokerage practice or any research method. Anyone citing it for technology findings would be citing a menu. The technology research it points to would need to be read directly.
